newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO LOOKING FOR TOUGH APPROACH AGAINST BORUSSIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO LOOKING FOR TOUGH APPROACH AGAINST BORUSSIA.

text.p: Monaco believe their new defensive resilience, embodied by the hard-tackling Emmanuel Petit, will help them through a tough UEFA Cup second round first leg clash away to Borussia Moenchengladbach on Tuesday.
Petit left one player with a fractured leg and another nursing a bruised thigh in Monaco's rough 0-0 draw away to Bastia on Saturday, sparking violent reaction from fans.

"We know combativity is primordial in European competition and I feel Bastia will have served us well," said Petit as Monaco prepare to face the German side that eliminated Arsenal of England in the previous round winning both legs 3-2.
"I don't know the Germans well, but we know that you have to impose yourselves pon them physically," he added.
Coach Jean Tigana, never on the winning side as a player against German sides including two World Cup semifinals, was happy with his players' performance in Corsica.

"That's what we'll need in Germany, to show that combativity and never relax because that's the Germans' strong point. They know better than anyone how to exploit the slightest weakness their opponents," Tigana said.
Monaco will be without suspended defender Franck Dumas and the injured Eric Di Meco, Marco Grassi and Enzo Scifo, while Borussia's Patrik Andersson is out with a foot injury.
Not all Germans won their first round battles, though.

Holders Bayern Munich crashed out to Valencia, who will be without unsettled Brazilian Romario -- dropped for their 2-0 win at Sevilla on Saturday -- for the trip to the Czech Republic to face Slavia Prague.
Captain and key defender Francisco Camarasa will also miss the game through injury.
Thomas Haessler, currently Germany's top player, plays against his former Italian club Roma, the first leg visitors.
Strongly South American influenced Roma, in fine form and convincing 3-0 winners over AC Milan at the weekend, will prove tough opposition for Karlsruhe.

Brazilian Aldair was at Roma when Haessler played there and he is now partnered in central defence by Roberto Trotta, who came to the club from Velez Sarsfield with fellow Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi.
Argentine striker Abel Balbo will also play with Uruguay's Daniel Fonseca likely to start on the bench, but Swedish midfielder Jonas Thern is doubtful with a toe injury.
Russian striker Sergei Kiryakov is back for Karlsruhe after a cheekbone fracture put him out for four weeks.
Kiryakov's compatriots Spartak Moscow, meanwhile, travel to Germany to face a Hamburg side fighting to get midfielder Harald Spoerl fit after a hip injury.
Hamburg will already be without the suspended Markus Schupp, sent off in a rough match against Glasgow Celtic in the previous round, and midfielder Bernd Hollerbach.
Spartak have Russian international playmaker Ilya Tsymbalar, back from injury and he was in sparkling form in the 3-1 win over Dyanmo in Saturday's Moscow derby.
But they have problems in defence and goalkeeper Ruslan Nigmatullin could lose his place to Alexander Filimonov.

Suspension has also ruled out Lazio captain Giuseppe Signori from the Roman side's home leg against Tenerife of Spain and Feyenoord's Henk Fraser from the Dutch team's trip to Barcelona to face Espanyol.
Lazio have Argentine defender Jose Chamot and midfielder Diego Fuser injured, while Tenerife have lost form in recent weeks and travel without Czech midfielder Pavel Hapal.
At Espanyol, some 500 visiting Feyenoord supporters are the chief concern. Dutch police were at their ground last week to inspect it for crowd control purposes.

Inter-Milan have selection problems of a different kind with an abundance of riches to chose from against Austrian minnows Casino Graz, who are in the second round of European competition for the first time and without suspended midfielder Gregor Poetscher.
